newsitem.title: FRANCE: Council of Europe raps 16 members on welfare.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe raps 16 members on welfare.

text.p: The Council of Europe on Monday criticised 16 of its member states for failing to provide proper welfare benefits, particularly for working women and children, as set down by the European Social Charter.

A report by the Council, which promotes democracy and human rights, rapped Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Denmark, France, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Malta, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and Turkey.
The report by a committee of independent experts said the most common shortcomings were an insufficient protection of women and children at work, and inequalities penalising foreigners.

In France, the report said there was no laws governing the hiring of a child by a parent. Children could thus work under the age of 16, the legal working age for France. The same was true of Ireland and Spain.
In countries including Austria, Italy and Norway, children under the age of 15 could work in the agriculture sector especially.
On the issue of women at work, the report criticsed Belgium for the absence of laws on pauses for breast-feeding at the workplace.
Post-natal leave lasted only two weeks in Great Britain and Denmark, and four weeks in Ireland, while the Charter provided for a minimum six weeks.

The report also said that foreigners legally settled in Britain or Sweden had no means of appealing against expulsion. Turkey and certain regions in Germany refused them welfare benefits, the report noted.
The report will be sent to the Council's committee of ministers, which can issue a series of recommendations by which member states are then bound.
